title: A shared annual SST error of 0.0372 K can remove mean fitted acceleration while it preserves the 1985-2024 trend
abstract: We tested how shared error can affect the mean of five corrected SST products at 60S-60N, January 1985 to June 2024. A linear program finds the smallest bounded shared error that removes the fitted quadratic coefficient while it preserves the linear trend. Each error has a zero 1991-2020 mean. The mean coefficient is 0.022854 K per decade squared and the linear trend is 0.14919 K per decade. An error constant within each year can remove the mean coefficient with a peak size of 0.03717 K, or 0.07434 K peak to peak. Every product-pair difference stays unchanged. If the error must also stay constant from 2005 onward, the minimum peak size is 0.06141 K. Five-year error levels give 0.04038 and 0.06581 K. Feasible error functions, dual bounds and an independent closed-form check support the results. These are sharp sensitivity bounds within the tested error classes, not evidence that such errors occurred. A conditional residual bootstrap still gives positive acceleration when shared error is fixed at zero. The result quantifies the need for independent record stability before the start of modern references. The period, mask, fixed predictors, corrected input series and synthetic shared-error assumption limit the conclusions.

display.caption: Synthetic annual shared errors that remove mean fitted SST acceleration, and the minimum peak error with a stable reference from each year. The linear trend stays fixed in the reference-date scan. These are sensitivity tests, not measured errors.

citations.reason: Uses verified exported corrected area means and detected dates. Quantifies its stated common-error limitation with sharp sensitivity bounds.
